status_note: Look-dev v2 of King Arthur (2026-09-29, wave LD): the H2.2 rev. 2 game model moved onto the UM material library v1 (docs/art-pipeline/material-library/README.md) for M_UM_Figure_v2: MatID (G8, index x 16 + 8, no mips), hero LUT 16 x 8 RGBA16F, UV1 in metres, EdgeMask, the new TeamAccent mask (docs/art-pipeline/material-library/team-accent.md: piping of the red cloth outside the gold border of the cloak (rev. 3, 5c-B0) + the belt; the gold border, the cloak and the tabard stay red / gold, the tabard carries no accent since rev. 2), steel = preset steel_blued with the hero tone measured on the concept relative to the unchanged stone and red cloth of the same frame. Rig, skeleton and geometry are those of the H2 bake run (appended from its work/h2-rig-authored.blend, checked against its FBX). Status: at most 'measured' (Blender only); UE import is the next stage.

lookdev.source_note: H2 bake run at H2.2 rev. 2 (commit 8a788343): work/h2-rig-authored.blend (rigged low-poly in the authored frame, saved by stage_rig just before its export), work/bake/*.npy, work/uv-*.npy|npz, work/phantom-points.npy (local, git-ignored) are read, never written. The committed H2 FBX and the H2.2 4K masters (sha256 in its textures-report) are the references of the read-back checks.

previous_sets.note: restored with git show <commit>:<runtime_2k path> into work/, sha256 checked; h22 = the 'previous' column of the frames, h2 = the orchestrator's visual reference for the steel (closest to the concept, 2026-09-29)

lookdev.ue_lut_config_note: proposal for the UE stage (same schema as merlin-h2-lookdev-ue-lut.json): stage ld_ue_inputs runs tools/art/material_library/lookdev_ue_inputs.py with it (read-only use of the generator) -> ue-inputs/ (LUT 16 x 16 DDS in the v2 layout, EdgeMask, debug ZoneID) to prove the outputs import the Merlin way; the UE stage owns and may change lut.ue_lookdev
lookdev.matid_px_note: as Merlin (LDM-4) and Medusa: MatID at the runtime atlas size 2K; Arthur's gold trims and embroidery are 3-8 texel lines at 2K

uv1.units: metres of the exported object (final frame; UE uu / 100)
uv1.rotate_note: no class of Arthur has a directional tile (wood / metal_forged are not used): every island is a similarity of its UV0 without rotation, so the detail normal blends in the UV0 tangent frame of the hero normal map
uv1.offset: island bounding-box centre to (0, 0) (smallest |UV1| for 16-bit UE UVs), as Merlin

zones.rules_note: soft class weights of the H2.1/H2.2 material pass (materials.py, painted BC, per part group; recomputed by ld_state): armour group -> steel_plate = metal x (1 - gold share) outside the blade part, blade = the same on the part with its own steel reference (tripo_part_10), gold = metal x gold share, lining = red (collar lining, red gems), belt = leather x (1 - red); cloth group (cloak, tabard) -> embroidery = gold x (1 - red) (the H2.1 'gold on cloth'), cloth = the rest; head group -> gold = strict gold in the crown / neck-ring regions, the rest split by the painted value into face_skin and hair (beard, brows, eyes); stone group -> base. The weights sum to 1 on every texel
zones.head_skin_note: measured 2026-09-29 on the painted BC of the head part (sRGB HSV, 4K): skin v p50 0.60 (hue 21, s 0.4-0.6), hair / beard v 0.20-0.23 (hue 21, s 0.2-0.4); the value separates them, the hue does not
zones.embroidery_note: Arthur's gold embroidery and hem bands are gold thread on cloth, as Merlin's (LDM-1): class silk, NOT metal and NOT team-dyed (H2.1/H2.2 made them metallic gold with the F0-mapped BC; the look-dev BC takes the painted colour back there)
zones.lining_note: red texels of the armour parts (the red collar / cloak lining at the gorget, red gems): cloth class, never team-dyed (TeamAccent 0 there)

envelope.note: 5c-B0: the gold border as a whole = the braid bands (embroidery components >= band_component_min_texels) + the red cloth between their threads: binary closing with a disk of 6 texels 4K (2.2 mm) inside the cloak, enclosed holes < 3000 texels filled. Measured 2026-09-30: radius 6 / 10 / 14 give 87.9 / 88.5 / 89.0 k texels 4K (stable); the border is one band ~21 mm wide. Never dyed

strip.note_rev3: rev. 3 (5c-B0, 2026-09-30, finding of look-dev C group B): the rev. 2 strip (red cloth within 14 mm of a band texel) also covered the red BETWEEN the braid threads; the threads are 1-2 texels wide, so the mips of the mask and of the BC turned the whole border into the team colour in UE (13-65 % of the silk pixels changed colour). Now the envelope of the border is never dyed and the accent is a piping of the red cloth OUTSIDE it, from gap_m to gap_m + width_m (final frame, 3D distance to an envelope texel with an agreeing normal), soft edges over feather_m. Chosen from gap 1.5 / 3 mm x width 5 / 7 / 9 mm by the mip_chain criteria (fixed before the edit): gap 1.5 mm lets the bilinear tail of mip 3 paint 10-12 % of the border, gap 3 mm keeps it <= 0.5 %; width 9 mm keeps the piping core >= 0.94 on mip 2 (K2 5x) and 0.78 on mip 3 (K2 1.6x)
strip.note: rev. 2 (mode strip): red cloth texels of the CLOAK (tripo_part_0) within width_m (final frame, 3D distance) of a gold border band (8-connected embroidery component of >= band_component_min_texels 4K texels: the hem and edge bands, not the small motifs) whose normal agrees (dot >= normal_agree_min: the other side of the cloth does not count); soft edge smoothstep over feather_m. The gold band itself is never dyed
strip.tabard_note: rev. 2 (2026-09-29, review defect): the tabard (tripo_part_5) is OUT of the strip. Its red field between the gold borders is only ~25-30 mm wide on the upper tabard and the lower knot panel is an embroidery component itself, so the rev. 1 strip (10 mm on both inner edges) dyed ~60-70 % of the visible tabard red (render red share 0.85 -> 0.33 / 0.31 with P1 / P2). The front panel of the hero is his main colour and stays red; the lost area is taken by a wider cloak strip (10 -> 14 mm, measured with tools probe: 12 mm gives 4.98 %, 14 mm 5.53 % of the figure)

red_parts.note: per part: <= max_core_share of the red cloth core texels of the part carry the accent (>= 0.5); render: the red share of the tabard pixels (tabard ID frame) with P1 / P2 >= render_red_share_min_ratio x the red share without dye, on the Cobble frames

belt.note: the leather belt of the torso (zone belt); the lion buckle and the studs are gold metal and stay out

team_accent.area_note: share of the figure's 3D surface (body + sword, without the base; texel area from the POS bake). The task range for Arthur was 5-12 %; rev. 3 (5c-B0) lowers it to 3-12 %: the 5.5 % of rev. 2 came from dyeing the red inside the gold border, which breaks the user rule (the gold borders are not dyed, the cloak stays red); the front readability of the team is carried by the ring / base shape of 5b-R

review_200uu.note: UE look-dev review frames (front / side / back at 200 uu)

mip_chain.note: 5c-B0, criteria fixed before the edit (reports/ld-5cb0-teamaccent.json#criteria): on every mip 0-3 (2K..256; K2 5x reads mip ~0.8, K2 1.6x ~2.5, a vertical surface at 55 deg up to ~3.3 without aniso), with box and Kaiser mips of the 2K mask: painted (value >= 0.25) <= 15 % of the gold border and of the cloak field (piping included), <= 1 % of the tabard and of every other zone; the piping core keeps a median >= 0.5 on mips 0-2. Mip 4 (128) is reported, not judged

team_dye_gain_rule.note: docs/art-pipeline/material-library/team-accent.md: TeamDyeGain per hero so that the median dyed accent albedo is ~0.8 x TeamColor and the 95th percentile stays <= 0.9 (brightest palette channel): gain = min(0.8 / Y_p50, 0.9 / (max channel x Y_p95)) over the accent texels (weight >= 0.5) of the final BC, Y clamped to [0.02, 0.8], rounded down to 0.5. Measured first with 5.5 (the Merlin/Medusa MIs): the P1 accent on Arthur's dark red cloth (Y ~0.03) read khaki-olive, not gold

team_accent.dye_note: the dye formula of M_UM_Figure_v2 (um_v2_core.hlsl): dyed = lerp(bc x Team, Team x Y(bc) x TeamDyeGain, TeamDye); bc = lerp(bc, dyed, mask x teamDyeAllowed). TeamAccent goes into the TeamMaskTexture slot (no graph change); TeamDye 1

roughness.note: Arthur: gold-thread embroidery (as Merlin, LDM-1): glossier than the wool, not the smooth silk plateau

silk.note: Arthur: embroidery = cloth with gold thread, NOT metal and NOT team-dyed (user rule 5c-A)

roughness.note: Arthur: satin blued plate. H2.2 rev. 2 (0.45-0.55) read slightly silvery already (orchestrator, 2026-09-29); the preset 0.37 [0.30, 0.45] (Metal038) is glossier still and mirrors the bright Cobble dome; variation = the preset's measured amplitude

steel_blued.note: baseColor (F0) and heroYmed are measured by ld_tone (concept tone relative to the stone and the red cloth)

gold_antique.note: baseColor (F0) chromaticity measured by ld_tone on the concept gold trims (white-balanced on the base stone); heroYmed measured

steel_polished.note: the blade: preset F0 (iron), heroYmed measured

steel_blued.why: engraving and the lighter gauntlets live in the bake luminance (H2.2 BC p10 / p90 = 0.47 / 1.51 of the median, gauntlets 1.5x the plate): the preset's +-15 % would flatten them; wear: the concept plate edges are gold trims, the EdgeMask of the Tripo normal also lights the engraving ridges -> 0.12 instead of 0.35 (a hint of bare iron on the ridges)

gold_antique.why: the gold trims carry painted relief (lion heads, knotwork): +-30 % instead of +-12 %

ue_lut_fields.note: LUT fields that the Blender override format of lookdev_ue_inputs.py (blender_overrides_to_lut) does not carry: they go into lut.ue_lookdev of the UE config (proposal king-arthur-h2-lookdev-ue-lut.json); the Blender emulation of this stage uses them. The luminance floors of the dielectric classes (UE-0 of Merlin) are added by ld_tone from the measured p2 of the bake

steel.candidates_note: F0 luminance candidates of steel_blued inside the oxide-film band 0.10-0.26 of the preset (validator: Y 0.05-0.35); preset typical Y 0.19. Each candidate is emulated (v2 metal path: F0 x clamp(Y(bake) / Ymed, 1 +- m) x cavity) and rendered in studio_env (ortho) and Cobble (K2 5x); the relative ratio is interpolated in log-log to the target
steel.target_note: relative steel ratio (steelcheck.relative_check: (Y_steel / Y_ref)_render / (Y_steel / Y_ref)_concept, references stone + red cloth, geometric mean, pooled front/side/back). Target 0.92 inside the +-15 % of H2.2 and toward H2 (0.81): the orchestrator saw H2 closest to the concept and H2.2 rev. 2 (1.04) slightly silvery
steel.rule: Y = max(Y at target_relative, Y at the Cobble floor cobble_range[0] of the mean steel / board over the K2 5x frames), capped at the Y of relative 1 + tolerance: the darkest steel that is neither black on the board nor outside the H2.2 relative tolerance (measured 2026-09-29: a metal cannot match H2 in both lights - H2's steel was a matt dielectric (metallic 0.07, roughness 0.71) that the Cobble dome lights diffusely; at relative 0.92 the v2 steel is 0.31-0.36 of the board = black)
steel.chroma: concept steel chromaticity / concept stone chromaticity x render stone chromaticity (the unchanged stone as the grey card of each frame), pooled over the views; F0 chromaticity = candidate chromaticity x (target / rendered), luminance kept

gold.note: gold_antique F0: chromaticity from the concept gold trims (white-balanced on the stone, as the steel); luminance: the relative ratio of the gold (the same formula as the steel, references stone + red cloth) interpolated over the candidates, clamped to Y >= 0.45 (metal rule LDD-7)

dielectric.note: as Merlin (lookdev_tone): gain = chroma x luma per zone, render exposure brought to the concept by the stone (k = concept stone / render stone per view), luma clamped; applied in linear light to the zone's BC texels at 4K (zone weights, 3 x 3 blur); |gain - 1| < dead_band in every channel keeps the H2.2 BC

belt.source: 5c-B0 (2026-09-30): UE look-dev C frames i2 (art/pipeline-candidates/ASSET-KING-ARTHUR-001/20260929-h2ld-ue/review/i2, LUT i2) against the concept; tools/art/material_library/ue_bc_feedback.py fit (zone belt, class pixels, weights reading 1 / board 0.5) -> ratio of the effective albedo (0.9895, 1.3245, 1.7819); gain = ue_bc_feedback.py gain on the 2K BC of the class (UE LUT i2 leather_worn: luminance [0.08, 0.45], maxChannel 0.9; 73 % of the belt texels sat on the 0.08 floor, so the BC gain is larger than the ratio)
belt.why: UE i2: the belt is off the concept on the reading exposure (-1 EV: Y 0.76, sat +0.185) and on the board (Y 0.92, sat +0.127) - a saturated baked BC below the class floor; the LUT has no saturation lever. Predicted after: -1 EV Y 0.91 / sat +0.03 / hue -0.6, board Y 1.09 / sat -0.03 (both in tolerance), other zones unchanged (reports/ld-5cb0-ue-feedback.json)

ue_feedback.note: per zone gain on the concept-tone BC (lookdev_tone.fit, blurred zone weights, after the dielectric gains): the UE frames are the reference of the final look, the Blender studio_env fit only the first step

concept_zones.note: boxes [x0, y0, x1, y1] in concept pixels (1190 x 1322) + an HSV filter of the pixel (sRGB); the concept is a lit render, only pixels of the zone's material inside a box are measured; overlays preview/ld_concept_zones_*.png. The steel zones are the H2.2 steel_check polygons (review_h22.steel_check.concept_zones of the source profile)

render.note: cameras = stage_compare of the H2 bake (ortho framed like the concept, K2 FOV 35 pitch -55 at 386 uu (5x) / 1207 uu (1.6x), close-ups on parts); lights: studio_env (the H2.1/H2.2 comparison light, the steel relative check) and Cobble calibrated to the W4-A anchor

cobble.source: unreal/Unmatched/Config/ArtBoards/S08ArtBoardProfiles.json lightProfiles.cobble-probe (read-only), as review_h22.lights.cobble of the source profile and review.h3.cobble of the Harpy H3 profile

exposure_calibration.method: W4-A anchor (cobble-probe sky.calibration): K1 board ROI p50 of Rec.709 luma of the 8-bit sRGB frame = 131.2; figure hidden, 40 m board of the cobblestone mean albedo, K1 camera; the exposure offset (stops, added to log2(1 / (1.2 * 2^EV100))) bisected until |p50 - target| <= tolerance (review_h3.py rev. 2, same numbers)
